minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District held its special district meeting to elect a moderator and act on three warrant articles, all funded from the surplus revenue account: back IRS/Medicare payments, Neptune R900 remote-read water meter gateways, and a new rubber-tired excavator for in-house project work. Residents questioned the makeup of the surplus account, including how much derives from the PAS lawsuit settlement, and all three articles were reported as passing by voice vote.

what_happened.line: Voters approved a surplus-account transfer to pay past-due employee Medicare payments, by voice vote.
Voters also approved a surplus-account transfer for Neptune remote-read water meter gateways at two tank sites, by voice vote.
Voters approved a third surplus-account transfer for a rubber-tired excavator for in-house water main work, by voice vote.
A resident asked how much of the surplus fund traces to the PAS lawsuit settlement; a commissioner said none of the night's articles drew on settlement money.
A commissioner said doing the Rolling Acres water main project in-house rather than through a contractor saved money, citing prevailing-wage costs avoided by district crews.

why_it_matters: All three approvals draw on the district's surplus revenue account rather than the regular water rate budget, so they don't change water bills directly but do reduce reserves the district holds.
The settlement-fund question bears on how much of that surplus a resident should expect stays available for future rate relief or capital work, separate from the PAS lawsuit money.
The in-house equipment purchase reflects a district choice to keep more infrastructure work off contract, which affects future project costs and staffing needs.
